structure: Part 4 of repos/trade-imports-ins-frontend at 406e300: the chrome around every page, sign-in, and the repo's own docs. Read in full: README.md; the seven docs under src/server/app/docs/ (README, features, architecture, services, add-a-page, testing; lighthouse.md is linked but not in this part's read list); src/server/app/shared/ (layout.njk, copy.js, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js, copy-leaves.js, kit.js, paths.js, error.njk, error-summary.njk); src/server/app/auth/unauthorised.njk; src/server/app/features/index.js and routes.js; src/server/router.js; src/server/auth/ (index.js, controller.js, stub-sign-in.js); src/plugins/auth.js and csrf.js; src/config/nunjucks/context/context.js; src/client/javascripts/application.js; fit/smoke.fit.spec.js and fit/sign-in.js; and the workspace page docs/repos/trade-imports-ins-frontend.md. To say what the error page and the sign-in redirects show, three small helpers the read files call were also read: src/server/common/helpers/errors.js (catchAll), src/auth/get-safe-redirect.js and src/auth/get-sign-out-url.js. Covered: the layout (title pattern, GOV.UK header, service navigation and which item is current, phase banner, back link, recoverable-error banner, journey strip, footer, skip link, no language toggle); every shared copy key in English and Welsh, plus the validator default messages; the error summary, the error page per status and the unauthorised page; the Defra ID routes (/auth/sign-in, /auth/sign-in-oidc, /auth/sign-out, /auth/sign-out-oidc, /auth/organisation), the session strategy and its redirect to sign-in, the stub-mode sign-in and sign-out routes (there is no stub sign-in form: it signs in on a GET); CSRF; the full route table and the dev/local-only spike; the single smoke test; and every rule the docs record about the dashboard, address book, handshake, copy, services, tests and boundaries. The workspace page disagrees with the repo in places (INS_MODE/AUTH_STUB_MODE vs STUB_MODE, Vite vs webpack, README described as template text); each is recorded as its own claim with a note, not reconciled.

claims.statement: GET /auth/sign-in requires Defra ID authentication, so a user without a Defra ID session is sent to Defra ID to sign in; once authenticated there, the route itself redirects to /.
When sign-in starts with a 'redirect' query parameter, its safe form is remembered in the session so the user can be returned there after Defra ID.
Sign-in goes to Defra ID over OIDC, asking for the openid and offline_access scopes and the service's client id, and passing the Defra ID service id and policy with a query response mode.
claims.quote: scope: ['openid', 'offline_access', config.get('defraId.clientId')],

claims.statement: The signed-in user's organisation is taken from the Defra ID token's currentRelationshipId, their CRN from its contactId, and their name from its first and last names.

crn: payload.contactId,

          organisationId: payload.currentRelationshipId

claims.statement: GET /auth/sign-in-oidc is the Defra ID callback the identity provider returns the user to after sign-in.

GET /auth/sign-out, for a signed-in user, ends the session (drops it from the cache and clears the cookie) and sends the user to Defra ID's sign-out page, which returns them to the service's configured post-logout address.
claims.quote:
signOutUrl.searchParams.set(
    'post_logout_redirect_uri',
    config.get('defraId.signOutRedirectUrl')
  )

claims.statement: GET /auth/sign-out for a user who is not signed in simply redirects to /.

GET /auth/sign-out-oidc is the Defra ID sign-out callback: for a signed-in user it checks the returned state when present, ends the session and redirects to Defra ID's sign-out page; otherwise it redirects to /.
GET /auth/organisation sends the user to Defra ID to choose their organisation again, pre-selecting the organisation given in an 'organisationId' query parameter when one is passed.
After organisation re-selection the user rejoins the service through the sign-in callback; if /auth/organisation itself is reached authenticated, it redirects to the remembered safe redirect or /.
claims.quote: // Should never be called as the user should no longer be authenticated with `defra-id` after initial sign in

claims.statement: A session is valid only while it is still in the server-side cache; when its token has expired the service refreshes it if token refresh is switched on, and otherwise treats the user as signed out.

claims.statement: Stub mode (STUB_MODE=true) switches data and sign-in together: it serves stub data and signs its own session, still enforces auth everywhere, and is refused in production.

Alternatively set `STUB_MODE=true`, which serves stub data and signs its
own session instead of doing the Defra ID OIDC exchange. Auth is still
enforced — only the external round-trip is bypassed — and the switch is
refused in production.

claims.statement: The application serves exactly nine routes, all behind sign-in: GET /; GET /address-book; GET and POST /address-book/add; GET /address-book/{id}; GET and POST /address-book/{id}/edit; GET and POST /address-book/{id}/delete.

The application registers nine routes, exactly as
[`routes.test.js`](../routes.test.js) pins them:

claims.statement: The six permanent page controllers are the dashboard and the address book's list, add, view, edit and delete pages.
claims.quote:
export const allRoutes = [
  ...dashboard.routes,
  ...addressBookList.routes,
  ...addressBookAdd.routes,
  ...addressBookView.routes,
  ...addressBookEdit.routes,
  ...addressBookDelete.routes
]

claims.statement: An address id in any /address-book/{id} URL must be a 24-character hex id; any other id gives a 404 page, not a validation error on the page.

every `{id}`
is validated by [`address-id-params.js`](../features/address-book/address-id-params.js)
as a 24-character hex Mongo ObjectId — a mismatch is a 404, not a validation
error on the page.

claims.statement: The country list is fetched on first use and cached for the life of the process; a failed load is retried on the next read and meanwhile shows the shared error page with a 503, and a reference-data outage does not stop the service starting.
claims.quote:
The list is fetched on the first read and cached at module
scope for the life of the process; a failed load leaves the cache unloaded
so the next read retries, and rejects with `Boom.serverUnavailable`, which
`catchAll` renders as the shared error page with a 503.
